title: Observation of High Doppler Velocity Wings in the Nascent Wind of R Doradus
question: What is the morpho-kinematics of the nascent wind of the AGB star R Doradus in the light of high Doppler velocity wings observed in five molecular spectral lines, and can they be interpreted as gas streams, stellar pulsations, or rotation?

recipe.goal: Coordinate system definition and data cube preparation
recipe.method: Retrieve pipeline-reduced continuum-subtracted data cubes from ALMA archive (and re-reduce SiO without continuum subtraction); set origin at continuum peak, refer Doppler velocities to LSR velocity of 7.0 km s^-1, and rotate sky coordinates so the x axis points 35 deg north of east and y axis 35 deg west of north.
key_parameters: x axis PA = 35 deg north of east; y axis PA = 35 deg west of north; V_LSR = 7.0 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Construct integrated Position-Velocity (P-V) maps, velocity spectra, and high-velocity moment/channel maps
recipe.method: Project data cubes onto the (x, Vz) and (y, Vz) planes by summing over y and x respectively; extract Doppler velocity spectra summed over a 1 arcsec radius circle; fit linear edges to the slow wind profile to measure end-point velocities; integrate emission for |Vz| > 7.5 km s^-1 to map high-velocity components and build 1 km s^-1 bin channel maps.
key_parameters: High velocity cut: |Vz| > 7.5 km s^-1; spectral extraction radius = 1 arcsec; channel map bin width = 1 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Characterize gas stream geometry, transverse spatial profiles, and acceleration
recipe.method: Define stream axes in P-V maps from origin to (x, y) = (0.1, -0.35) arcsec at Vz = -20 km s^-1 (blue-shifted) and (-0.1, 0.1) arcsec at Vz = 20 km s^-1 (red-shifted); integrate intensity above slow-wind end-point velocities (|Vz| > 7.0, 8.3, 6.2, 6.0 km s^-1 for CO, SiO, SO, SO2) and fit 1D Gaussians to transverse x and y profiles with respect to stream axes; compute beam-deconvolved widths and mean projected acceleration.
assumptions: Distance to R Doradus is ~59 pc (converting angular scales to au); illustrative stream length of 60 au (or mean distance 30 au) along the line of sight to estimate angles; z approximated as a linear function of Vz.

recipe.method: Repeat the analysis of SiO(8-7) using two datasets with different antenna configurations without subtracting continuum in the uv plane; extract Doppler velocity distributions for |Vz| > 8 km s^-1 within circular apertures of R < 1.5 arcsec and R < 0.3 arcsec.
key_parameters: |Vz| > 8 km s^-1; aperture radii R < 1.5 arcsec and R < 0.3 arcsec

recipe.goal: Evaluate physical interpretations (symmetric streams, rotation, stellar pulsations)
recipe.method: Calculate geometric constraints for symmetric streams from projected extents (30 au blue-shifted, 10 au red-shifted); extrapolate literature Keplerian and solid-body rotation models to a 20 km s^-1 velocity to test consistency with observed spatial scales.
assumptions: Rotation velocity of 12 km s^-1 at 6 au (Homan et al. 2018b) for Keplerian test; solid body rotation of 1.0 ± 0.1 km s^-1 at 1.9 au (Vlemmings et al. 2018) for solid body test.

score_reason: The paper uses public ALMA archival data (mostly standard pipeline products) and performs straightforward geometric projections, velocity cuts, and 1D Gaussian fits with clearly stated coordinate rotations and velocity thresholds. However, software versions, exact spatial integration windows for the summed P-V maps, and specific execution block selections for project 2013.1.00166.S are not explicitly stated.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA data are public in the archive (projects 2013.1.00166.S and 2017.1.00824.S), standard pipeline cubes can be used directly for the main analysis, and the key quantitative results (line peak intensities, slow-wind terminal velocities, high-velocity wing reach, projected acceleration, deconvolved stream widths, and continuum flux) are straightforward to re-measure.
